n: By January 19, 1841, the Saints had found refuge at Nauvoo, Illinois, after being expelled from Missouri. The Lord accepts Joseph’s offering and explains he raised Joseph up to show divine wisdom through humble, “weak” people.

f.w: the weak things of the earth

n: Joseph is to issue a formal proclamation of the gospel and of Nauvoo as a stake—a “cornerstone of Zion”—to be refined and beautiful like a palace.

f.g: Nauvoo was to be a central, foundational stake for the gathering.

f.w: after the similitude of a palace

n: The proclamation is to go to world rulers, the U.S. president-elect (William Henry Harrison), state governors, and all nations.

f.g: William Henry Harrison had been elected in November 1840 and took office in March 1841.

n: It should be written with meekness and under the Holy Ghost’s influence.
The Spirit will show Joseph what lies ahead for these rulers.

f.g: Befall = happen to.

n: The Lord will call on rulers to pay attention to Zion, because the appointed time to favor her has come.

f.w: the set time has come to favor her

n: Speak boldly and without fear; earthly rulers are like grass and fading flowers. The warning leaves them without excuse.
If they reject the Lord’s servants, at his coming they will be counted with the hypocrites in sorrow and regret.

f.w: unveil the face of my covering

n: Yet the Lord will soften many rulers’ hearts, so the Saints will find favor and the Gentiles will help lift up Zion.

f.g: Grace here = favor.

n: The Lord’s coming will be sudden; where will his people find safety? The question urges preparation.

f.w: in an hour when ye think not

n: Echoing Isaiah, kings are invited to bring their wealth to help God’s people and build up Zion.

f.w: with your gold and your silver

n: Robert B. Thompson, Joseph’s clerk, is to help write the proclamation. He died later that year at age 30.

f.g: Church clerk and editor of the Times and Seasons; he died in August 1841.

n: If he follows Joseph’s counsel and stays faithful, he will be richly blessed and great in God’s eyes.

f.g: A great number; abundance.

n: But the Lord will hold him accountable for his stewardship.

f.g: A responsibility entrusted by God, for which one must give an account.

n: Hyrum Smith is praised: the Lord loves him for his integrity and love of right. Hyrum was known for unwavering loyalty.
John C. Bennett, a recent convert who was then mayor-elect of Nauvoo, is to help—with blessings conditional on accepting counsel.

f.g: Bennett later fell into serious immorality, was excommunicated in 1842, and became a bitter opponent; the condition here proved significant.

n: The Lord accepts Bennett’s work “if he continue.” Promises in scripture are often conditional on faithfulness.

f.w: which I accept if he continue

n: Lyman Wight is to keep preaching for Zion humbly; the Lord will carry him “as on eagles’ wings.”
When Lyman finishes, the Lord will receive him as he has received David Patten, Edward Partridge, and Joseph Smith Sr.—who sits with Abraham. A glimpse into the faithful dead.

f.g: The Prophet’s father, first Patriarch of the Church, died September 1840.

n: George Miller is praised as honest and trustworthy, with a love for the Lord’s testimony.
George Miller is called as a bishop to receive consecrated offerings and bless the poor.

f.g: Offerings dedicated to the Lord’s work.

n: George Miller, Lyman Wight, John Snider, and others are to build a boarding house on a site Joseph will show them.

f.w: build a house unto my name

n: It is to be a fine inn where travelers can rest, find health and safety, and ponder the Lord’s word.
The house must be kept clean and holy under its appointed manager, or the Lord will not dwell there.

f.w: the governor which shall be appointed
f.g: Governor = manager or overseer.

n: All Saints from far away are to gather.

f.w: let all my saints come from afar

n: Messengers should invite people to bring precious materials and antiquities to build the temple—recalling how Israel brought fine materials for the tabernacle and Solomon’s temple.

f.w: the box tree, and the fir tree, and the pine tree

f.g: Ancient objects or relics.

n: Iron, copper, brass, zinc, and precious things will help build a house for the Most High.

f.w: build a house to my name

n: There is no place on earth where the Lord can restore the “fulness of the priesthood.” Higher ordinances require a temple.

f.g: The highest priesthood blessings, received through temple ordinances such as the endowment and sealing.

n: There is no baptismal font for baptisms for the dead—an ordinance Joseph had introduced in August 1840.

f.w: baptized for those who are dead

n: This ordinance belongs in the temple and is acceptable elsewhere only while the Saints are too poor to build one. Early proxy baptisms were done in the Mississippi River.

f.w: only in the days of your poverty
f.g: Before the Nauvoo Temple font was dedicated in November 1841, these baptisms were done in rivers.

n: The Lord gives a grace period: while they build, baptisms outside the temple are acceptable.

f.g: An appointed period of grace.

n: After that time, such baptisms won’t be accepted, and if the Saints fail to build, they will be rejected as a church with their dead. The temple was essential.

f.w: rejected as a church, with your dead

n: Baptism for the dead was instituted before the world was created and belongs in God’s house.

f.w: from before the foundation of the world

n: The temple holds the keys of the priesthood that bring honor and glory.
After this time, baptisms for the dead done by scattered members outside the temple won’t be accepted.

f.g: Members living away from the central gathering place.

n: Such baptisms belong in Zion, its stakes, and Jerusalem—the appointed places of refuge where temples would be.

f.w: in Zion, and in her stakes, and in Jerusalem

n: How can washings be acceptable except in a house built to the Lord’s name? Ordinances need sacred space.

f.g: Ritual cleansing ordinances; compare the Mosaic washings of priests.

n: This is why Moses built a portable tabernacle and Israel later a temple: to reveal ordinances hidden since before the world.

f.w: I commanded Moses that he should build a tabernacle

n: A long list of temple ordinances and functions—anointings, washings, baptisms for the dead, solemn assemblies, offerings by the sons of Levi, and holy-place revelations—all belong to the Lord’s house.

f.w: memorials for your sacrifices by the sons of Levi

f.g: Revelations or divine communications.
Probably citizens or communities of Zion.

n: Build this house so the Lord may reveal his ordinances in it.
The Lord will reveal things hidden since before creation, belonging to this final dispensation.

f.g: Condescend graciously; be willing.

f.w: kept hid from before the foundation of the world

n: Joseph will be shown everything about the temple—its priesthood and its site.

f.w: I will show unto my servant Joseph all things

n: The site they had already considered—on the bluff overlooking the Mississippi—is the Lord’s choice.

f.w: the spot which I have chosen
f.g: The Nauvoo Temple was built on a bluff above the city; it was rebuilt on the same site and dedicated in 2002.

n: If they work with all their might, the Lord will make the spot holy.

f.g: Make sacred; set apart for holy use.

n: If the Saints follow the Lord and his appointed leaders, they will not be moved from their place.

f.w: they shall not be moved out of their place

n: If they don’t listen, they won’t be blessed, because they defile holy ground and ordinances. The Saints were in fact driven from Nauvoo in 1846.

f.g: Formal grants or founding documents; here, sacred authorizations.

n: A clear warning: building a temple without obedience won’t bring the promised blessings.

f.w: I will not perform the oath

n: Disobedience turns blessings into curses—by their own choices.

f.g: Foolish acts.

n: A comforting principle: when people try with all their might to do God’s work but enemies stop them, God accepts their offering and no longer requires the work of them.

f.g: It is fitting or proper for me.

n: The guilt falls on those who obstructed God’s work, as long as they refuse to repent.

f.w: unto the third and fourth generation

n: This is why the Lord accepted the efforts of those commanded to build Zion and a temple in Jackson County who were prevented by enemies.
Judgment rests on those who drove them out and refuse to repent.
This is given as comfort for all who have been hindered by enemies from doing God’s work.

f.g: Consolation = comfort in loss or disappointment.

n: The Lord will save all the pure-hearted Saints killed in Missouri.

f.w: slain in the land of Missouri

n: Again the command: build a temple here in Nauvoo, to prove faithfulness and receive honor, immortality, and eternal life.
The boarding house is to bear the Lord’s name, and Joseph’s family should have a place in it permanently.

f.w: let my name be named upon it
f.g: Dedicated to the Lord’s purposes.

n: Joseph’s anointing and blessing extend to his descendants.
The Lord repeats to Joseph the Abrahamic promise: through you and your seed all the families of the earth will be blessed.

f.w: In thee and in thy seed shall the kindred of the earth be blessed

n: So Joseph’s family will have a place in that house forever.

f.g: Emma Smith and her family did live in the partly finished Nauvoo House after Joseph’s death.

n: It shall be called the Nauvoo House—a pleasant inn where travelers can rest and admire Zion and the temple.

f.g: Never completed as planned; a portion was later finished as a home and still stands in Nauvoo.

n: Travelers may also receive counsel from leaders who are like noted plants and watchmen on the walls.
George Miller, Lyman Wight, John Snider, and Peter Haws are to organize as a quorum with a president to build the Nauvoo House.

f.g: The Nauvoo House Association was chartered by the Illinois legislature in 1841.

n: They should draft a constitution to sell shares of stock to finance the building.

f.g: Shares of ownership sold to raise money.

n: Shares must cost at least $50, and no one person may hold more than $15,000—preventing any single investor from controlling it.

f.g: A substantial sum in 1841, roughly a month or two of a laborer’s wages.

n: The maximum is repeated for emphasis: no more than $15,000 from one man.

f.g: Firm limits to protect fairness.

n: The minimum is repeated as well.

f.g: The minimum share price.

n: Stock is given only on actual payment—no credit or promises.

f.w: at the time he receives stock
f.g: Payment up front was required, likely to avoid the debt problems of Kirtland.

n: Shares are proportional to payment; no payment, no stock.

f.g: Equal to the amount paid in.

n: Stock belongs to the buyer and his heirs as long as they choose to keep it.

f.g: Transfer ownership legally.

n: The managers must use the money only for the Nauvoo House.

f.g: Take or use for a particular purpose.

n: Misusing funds without consent requires fourfold repayment, or the managers will be cursed and removed. God cannot be mocked.
Joseph himself is bound by the same limits—no special exemption for the Prophet.

f.g: The rules apply equally to all.

n: Others had asked what the Lord wanted of them; he now answers them individually.

f.w: they have asked it at my hands

n: Vinson Knight, a bishop, may invest in the house for his family.

f.g: A bishop in Nauvoo; he died in 1842.

n: Vinson should speak loudly for the poor and needy; his offerings will be accepted, unlike Cain’s.
His family should take heart; the Lord has chosen him and will forgive his sins.

f.w: I will forgive all his sins

n: Hyrum may invest as he sees fit.

f.g: As he thinks best.

n: Isaac Galland, who sold land to the Saints in Iowa and Illinois, may invest; the Lord loves him for his help and forgives his sins.

f.g: A land agent who helped the Saints acquire land near Commerce (Nauvoo) and joined the Church in 1839.

n: Galland is to be ordained by William Marks and travel with Hyrum on business Joseph assigns.

f.w: ordained by my servant William Marks
f.g: Marks was Nauvoo stake president.

n: William Marks may invest.
Henry G. Sherwood, a high councilor, may invest.
William Law, soon to be a counselor in the First Presidency, may invest.

f.g: He later turned against Joseph and helped publish the Nauvoo Expositor in 1844.

n: Law should not take his family back east to Kirtland. The Lord will one day build up Kirtland but has a scourge prepared for its current inhabitants.

f.g: A whip; a source of severe punishment or affliction.

n: Almon Babbitt, presiding in Kirtland, is rebuked for setting up his own counsel against the First Presidency and leading people to worship a “golden calf”—a false priority.

f.g: Seeks ambitiously.

n: No one who came to Nauvoo to keep God’s commandments should leave.

f.g: Trying, attempting.

n: Whether they live or die, let them do so in the Lord. The faithful dead rest from labor yet continue their work.

f.w: if they die let them die unto me

n: William Law worried about malaria and illness in swampy Nauvoo. The Lord says: trust me; keep the commandments, and even sickness will turn to your glory.

f.g: Malaria and other fevers were common in Nauvoo’s marshy riverfront.

f.w: If ye love me, keep my commandments

f.g: Contribute or result.

n: Law is to preach joyfully in nearby towns—Warsaw, Carthage, Burlington, and Madison—then await further instruction at conference.

f.g: Warsaw and Carthage were Illinois towns later hostile to the Saints; Joseph was killed at Carthage in 1844.

n: He should follow Joseph’s counsel, help the poor, and help publish Joseph’s new Bible translation.

f.w: the new translation of my holy word
f.g: Joseph Smith’s inspired revision of the Bible (JST); it was not fully published during his lifetime.

n: If he does, he will be blessed and his children will never beg for bread.

f.w: his seed be found begging bread

n: William Law is to replace Hyrum as counselor in the First Presidency so Hyrum can become Patriarch—an office his father held and blessed him to inherit.

f.g: Presiding Patriarch to the Church, who gives patriarchal blessings.

f.w: by blessing and also by right
f.g: Joseph Smith Sr., the first Patriarch, blessed Hyrum as his successor before dying in 1840.

n: Hyrum will hold the keys of patriarchal blessings for all the Church.
Those Hyrum blesses will be blessed; what he binds on earth will be bound in heaven—sealing power.

f.w: whatsoever he shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven

n: Hyrum is also made a prophet, seer, and revelator to the Church alongside Joseph.

f.w: a prophet, and a seer, and a revelator

n: Hyrum is to work together with Joseph and receive the blessings and priesthood once held by Oliver Cowdery—the “Second Elder” and Associate President, who had left the Church in 1838.

f.g: Oliver had been Associate President and second witness with Joseph of key restorations; he returned to the Church in 1848.

n: Hyrum will testify of what the Lord shows him, and his name will be honored forever. He died beside Joseph as a fellow witness.
William Law should also receive keys to ask and receive. If humble and without guile, the Comforter will teach him all truth and give him words in the moment.

f.w: in the very hour, what he shall say

n: Signs will follow him: healing, casting out devils, and protection from poison—as Jesus promised believers.
He will be protected from serpents and soar in his thoughts like an eagle.
If the Lord wills him to raise the dead, he should not hold back his voice.
Law should preach boldly with joy and hosannas to God on his throne.
The Lord has a special mission for William and Hyrum; Joseph is needed at home.

f.g: Stay home.

n: Sidney Rigdon, often sick and discouraged after Missouri, is invited to rise up, fulfill his calling as Joseph’s counselor, and humble himself.

f.w: if my servant Sidney will serve me
f.g: Sidney had suffered greatly in Missouri and was in poor health.

n: If Sidney offers an acceptable offering and stays with the Saints, he will be healed and again be a spokesman.
He should move his family near Joseph.

f.g: Settle his household.

n: In his travels he should warn the world like a trumpet to flee the coming wrath.
Sidney and William Law should help Joseph write the proclamation to the kings.

f.w: a solemn proclamation unto the kings of the earth

n: Sidney should not move east but relocate as directed.

f.g: Pennsylvania, Ohio, and the eastern states.

n: He should not look for safety outside Nauvoo. After Joseph’s death Sidney did leave for Pittsburgh.

f.g: Nauvoo is often said to mean “beautiful” or “beautiful place” in Hebrew.

n: Even now, if Sidney listens, all will be well with him.

f.w: it shall be well with him

n: Amos Davies is told to invest in the Nauvoo House.

f.g: A Nauvoo storekeeper and postmaster.

n: If he wants a share, he must follow Joseph’s counsel and work with his own hands to earn people’s trust.
Faithful in a few things, he will rule over many.
So he should humble himself to be exalted.

f.w: abase himself that he may be exalted

n: Robert D. Foster, a doctor and builder, is to build a house for Joseph as contracted.

f.g: Later a leading opponent of Joseph and co-publisher of the Nauvoo Expositor.

n: He must repent of folly, be charitable, stop doing evil, and stop harsh speech.
He should also invest in the Nauvoo House.

f.w: the quorum of the Nauvoo House
f.g: The board managing the building.

n: If he follows the counsel of Joseph, Hyrum, William Law, and other leaders, all will be well with him forever.
Only believers in the Book of Mormon and the revelations may invest in the Nauvoo House.

f.w: a believer in the Book of Mormon
f.g: Keeping the project in the hands of committed members.

n: Anything more or less than this comes from evil and brings curses.

f.w: more or less than this cometh of evil

n: The Nauvoo House committee should be fairly paid, at wages they agree on.

f.g: Fair payment.

n: Stockholders share the cost of wages if needed; otherwise the workers’ labor counts as stock.

f.g: Pay his fair share.

n: Now the Lord lists the officers of the Melchizedek Priesthood—named after the Son’s holy order—for Nauvoo.

f.w: after the order of mine Only Begotten Son

n: First, Hyrum Smith as Patriarch, holding sealing blessings by the Holy Spirit of Promise, which seals the faithful up to redemption.
Joseph is presiding elder over the whole Church—translator, revelator, seer, and prophet.

f.w: a translator, a revelator, a seer, and prophet

n: Sidney Rigdon and William Law are Joseph’s counselors; together they form the First Presidency.
Brigham Young is President of the Quorum of the Twelve—a calling that made him the senior leader after Joseph’s death.
The Twelve hold keys to open the kingdom everywhere and send the word to every creature.

f.w: the four corners of the earth

n: The other apostles are named. Several, like John Taylor and Wilford Woodruff, later became Church Presidents.

f.g: Joseph’s younger brother; he was later excommunicated (1845).

n: David Patten, killed in 1838, keeps his priesthood in the next life, but another may fill his calling. Priesthood continues beyond death.

f.w: his priesthood no man taketh from him

n: A high council is given to Nauvoo, the cornerstone stake.
The high councilors are named. Seymour Brunson had died; Aaron Johnson is to replace him.

f.w: Seymour Brunson I have taken unto myself
f.g: Brunson died in August 1840; Joseph first taught baptism for the dead publicly at his funeral.

n: Don Carlos Smith, Joseph’s youngest brother, is to preside over a quorum of high priests.

f.g: Don Carlos Smith died in August 1841 at age 25.

n: The high priests’ quorum prepares men to serve as stake presidents and other standing (local) officers.

f.g: Resident, local leaders, as opposed to traveling ministers.

n: They may travel, but their main calling is to preside locally.
Amasa Lyman and Noah Packard are his counselors.

f.g: Later an apostle.

n: John A. Hicks, Samuel Williams, and Jesse Baker preside over the elders, who are mainly local ministers.

f.g: Local, resident ministers.

n: Seven presidents are named over the seventies. Joseph Young was Brigham Young’s older brother.
The seventies are traveling elders sent by the Twelve to testify worldwide and prepare the way for the Lord.

f.w: prepare a way before my face

n: The difference: seventies travel continually; elders preside over local branches from time to time.
Vinson Knight, Samuel H. Smith, and Shadrach Roundy are to preside over the bishopric, as explained in the Doctrine and Covenants.

f.g: Joseph’s brother and one of the Eight Witnesses; he died in July 1844, weeks after the martyrdom.

f.w: the book of Doctrine and Covenants
f.g: The 1835 edition, which contained the revelation on priesthood (now D&C 107).

n: Presidents and counselors of priests, teachers, deacons, and the stake are also named or provided for.

f.g: Nauvoo presiding priest; he also helped build the temple.

n: These offices and keys are given to help govern, minister, and perfect the Saints.
The Saints must sustain or reject these names at general conference—the principle of common consent.

f.g: Common consent: members vote to sustain leaders.

n: Rooms should be prepared in the temple for these priesthood quorums.

f.w: prepare rooms for all these offices in my house
f.g: The Nauvoo Temple’s upper floors included offices and rooms for councils.
